html:
Short answer: good stage lighting starts with even light on faces, then adds back and side light for depth, then effects. For churches and venues that stream, lighting must look right on camera, not just in the room.

The three layers

  1. Front light: soft, even light on faces from about 45 degrees.
  2. Back and side light: separates people from the background and adds depth.
  3. Effects and colour: LED washes, moving heads and haze for atmosphere.

Fixtures

  • LED wash and par lights: efficient, low heat, colour mixing.
  • Profile spots: sharp, controlled light for speakers and pulpits.
  • Moving heads: movement and effects for worship and events.

Control

A lighting console or software with saved scenes lets volunteers run services and events with one press. We set up scenes for the common moments in your programme.

Lighting for cameras

Cameras need more even light and the right colour temperature. Plan lighting together with your live streaming set-up where relevant.

faqs.a: For most venues, yes. They use far less power, run cooler, last longer and mix colours without gels.
